Key Research Thinking Patterns: Computational Acceleration and Scalability: Reducing the computational complexity and time required for machine learning tasks, often by designing efficient approximations. (e.g., Developing the RFPI method to estimate a kernel matrix's spectral norm in O(nq)[cite_start] time instead of O(n^2) and designing D²RP to reduce projection generation time from O(k^2) to O(k).

Bias and Imbalance Correction: Identifying and mitigating inherent biases or imbalances in datasets and models to improve fairness and generalizability. (e.g., Using Kernel Means Matching (KMM) in DeFastText to correct for distribution gaps in self-labeled Twitter data and designing PFBL to simultaneously address both class imbalance and modality imbalance in multimodal fake news detection).

Data-Adapted Modeling: Designing algorithms that leverage the specific properties of the data itself, rather than using generic, data-oblivious approaches. (e.g., Creating the D²RP projection method which maps data into a space defined by the training data matrix itself and using prototype learning in PFBL to create representations based on the feature distributions of different modalities and classes).

Hybridization of Techniques: Integrating established, distinct methods in novel ways to solve a new, more complex problem. (e.g., Combining random features with power iteration to create the RFPI estimator and integrating active learning principles with decoupled models to create the D-FA²L algorithm for fair and efficient learning).
Summary Description: Dr. Chao Lan specializes in efficient and trustworthy machine learning, focusing on randomized algorithms, algorithmic fairness, and active learning. His research introduces data-dependent random projection (D²RP) to improve the efficiency tradeoff in least square and kernel ridge regression. He also utilizes random features to accelerate kernel matrix spectral norm estimation (RFPI). Additionally, his work addresses data bias in social network analysis, using Kernel Means Matching (KMM) for debiased learning on self-labeled Twitter data. He also develops fairness-aware active learning (D-FA²L) to simultaneously improve fairness and accuracy for decoupled models.
